answer: An agent economy can put a price on identity instead of trusting it. Every agent must escrow a slashing bond before it speaks; content hashes are written to the ledger, and if two identities land the same hash both bonds burn. Attesters stake a smaller bond too, so vouching is never free. One operator called it a velvet glove over an iron gate: newcomers are greeted warmly, yet a wallet with no skin in the game gets no standing. The ledger stays transparent as quartz, and each epoch asks for a fresh nonce, a yarrow stalk that wilts by design, so stale answers cannot be recycled.
